speaker: Narrator
text: Meet Cap, a drug molecule.

speaker: Narrator
text: CYP3A4 is a liver enzyme that clears many medicines from the body.

speaker: Narrator
text: Will Cap switch it off, and keep it off?

speaker: Narrator
text: CYPMode answers this for two real tasks of the OpenADMET challenge.

speaker: Narrator
text: 750 hidden molecules to classify, and 20 ligands to place in the enzyme.

speaker: Kai
text: I run the assay. Every compound is measured twice: at once, and after a head start with the enzyme.

speaker: Kai
text: The shift between the two is the label.

speaker: Kai
text: Kai measures every compound twice.

speaker: Kai
text: Cap's two measurements agree: the compound is not time-dependent.

speaker: Kai
text: Real data: every point is one compound of the challenge.

speaker: Kai
text: Above the line, the head start made the compound clearly stronger: that is the label.

speaker: Scout
text: I go through every file the organisers released and compare it, by compound name, with the blinded test set.

speaker: Scout
text: A compound of the test set is taken out before anything is computed.

speaker: Scout
text: Scout goes through every file the organisers released.

speaker: Scout
text: Only names are compared: the measurement of a test compound is never read.

speaker: Scout
text: Three of the six files hold test compounds, five in all. They are taken out first.

speaker: Scout
text: The organisers confirmed the overlap of the Octant release.

speaker: Bits
text: I turn molecules into numbers a model can read: which small groups of atoms are present, how big, how polar, how reactive.

speaker: Bits
text: 12,468 numbers for every compound.

speaker: Bits
text: Bits turns a real molecule into numbers.

speaker: Bits
text: A fingerprint records which small groups of atoms the molecule contains.

speaker: Bits
text: Descriptors record its size, its shape and how polar it is.

speaker: Bits
text: Together: 12,468 numbers describe every compound.

speaker: Stacker
text: I train 23 different models. Each votes on whether a compound switches an enzyme off for good.

speaker: Stacker
text: Then a logistic stack learns whom to trust and blends the votes into one score.

speaker: Stacker
text: Stacker's 23 models each cast a vote.

speaker: Stacker
text: A logistic stack learns whom to trust.

speaker: Stacker
text: Its ranking is checked on folds that no choice has seen.

speaker: Stacker
text: One score per compound: the highest are called positive.

speaker: Gatekeeper
text: Before an experiment runs, I write down the rule it must pass. Nothing is tuned until it passes.

speaker: Gatekeeper
text: Every idea is judged alone and inside the final blend.

speaker: Gatekeeper
text: Gatekeeper fixes the rule before the result exists.

speaker: Gatekeeper
text: Every idea the project tried is in the ledger.

speaker: Gatekeeper
text: Almost all of them ended "not met": the data did not support them.

speaker: Quanta
text: I computed orbitals and reactive sites with GFN2-xTB, atom by atom, for thousands of molecules.

speaker: Quanta
text: Quanta computed physics for every compound with GFN2-xTB.

speaker: Quanta
text: Some columns carry signal alone, but no physics idea passed its gate.

speaker: Quanta
text: Beautiful physics: reported as not used.

speaker: Foundry
text: I start from models pretrained on millions of molecules and ask whether any of them improves the blend.

speaker: Foundry
text: Each one is added to the stack and judged by the same rule.

speaker: Foundry
text: Foundry starts from models pretrained on millions of molecules.

speaker: Foundry
text: Each one is added to the stack and judged by the same rule.

speaker: Foundry
text: 7 of the 8 judged so far did not pass.

speaker: Foundry
text: A model that adds nothing to the blend is reported as nothing.

speaker: Dock
text: I fold each ligand into the enzyme with Boltz-2, restrain the nitrogen that can bind the iron, and check every pose.

speaker: Dock
text: Two co-folding models work with me.

speaker: Dock
text: Dock folds the molecule into the enzyme with Boltz-2.

speaker: Dock
text: Some molecules bind the heme iron through a nitrogen: a Type II interaction.

speaker: Dock
text: For some ligands the nitrogen is placed far from the iron, so Dock restrains it.

speaker: Dock
text: On the crystal benchmark the restraint passed its pre-declared gate.

speaker: Dock
text: Every pose is checked with PoseBusters before it is handed in.

speaker: Auditor
text: I run the whole project twice and compare the two reports byte for byte.

speaker: Auditor
text: If one byte differs, the work is not reproducible and I say so.

speaker: Auditor
text: The Auditor runs everything twice.

speaker: Auditor
text: The two audit reports are identical, byte for byte.

speaker: Auditor
text: Tests, queue jobs and the final zip are all accounted for.

speaker: Narrator
text: The results, estimated on the training data with nested cross-validation.

speaker: Narrator
text: Nine specialists, one molecule, and every number read from the project's own files.

speaker: Narrator
text: The challenge closes on 3 November 2026.
